policy_title: End Gender Price Gap and Period Poverty
stated: Tackle the specific economic barriers facing women by: Ending the gender price gap so that women are not charged more than men for practically identical products or services marketed at them. Ending period poverty by introducing a right for anyone who needs them to access free period products.

source.quote: Tackle the specific economic barriers facing women by: Ending the gender price gap so that women are not charged more than men for practically identical products or services marketed at them. Ending period poverty by introducing a right for anyone who needs them to access free period products.

bearing_set.reason: Both measures directly reduce costs borne by women: eliminating gender-premium pricing on everyday consumer goods lowers real expenditure, and free period products remove a recurrent essential cost, with the largest gains for lower-income households.

The gender price gap element creates a legal prohibition on gender-based price discrimination in commercial products, directly constituting an equal-treatment protection on the basis of sex — a core O9 indicator.

membership_note: Two clean bearings: O2 for the direct cost-of-essentials effect on women, O9 for the equal-treatment/anti-discrimination dimension. O14 (rich-poor gap) is not engaged materially — this is a gender equity rather than income-distribution measure. O12 is not materially affected — the public cost of a period-products entitlement is real but unlikely to move the debt-sustainability path at a macro level. O11 is not in scope (no tax change). O10 is not meaningfully engaged — business price-regulation is well outside the speech/surveillance/bodily-autonomy core of that fundamental.
